caseStudy.subtitle: A wearable that knows where you are, and a companion app that tells the people you trust when you leave a safe area.

facts.label: Tools
facts.value: Raspberry Pi, Python, Eagle (PCB), Fusion 360, Figma, FlutterFlow

body: LOCIT is a location-tracking necklace meant to improve personal safety. It tracks the wearer’s location and sends an alert when they enter or leave a predefined area.
problem.needs: Who this was for and what situation prompted it, in Victoria’s words.

why.needs: Why personal location safety mattered to the team or the users they had in mind. Cite any source used.

body: I defined the product vision and requirements, and translated user needs into technical specs for GPS tracking, geofencing and facial recognition.
I led the team through ideation, prototyping, user testing and the capstone milestones, and designed the companion app in Figma before it was built in FlutterFlow.
role.needs: Team size and who owned the hardware, firmware and app build.

body: The device ran on a Raspberry Pi. Eagle was used for PCB design, and the enclosure was modelled in Fusion 360 and printed in PLA.
The companion app was designed in Figma and built in FlutterFlow.
decisions.needs: The reasoning behind each choice and what alternatives were considered.

body: The companion app screens below were built in FlutterFlow: a sign-in screen, a live location map, and a geofence screen that warns when the wearer is out of bounds.

figures.alt: Three phone screens from the LOCIT companion app: a teal sign-in screen reading Stay Connected, a campus map with a red location pin, and a geofence screen showing a Warning: User out of bounds dialog.
